advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the verify-identity unblock to the two named root causes (exempt reducer-ignored sidecar event types + have the gate re-resolve null-ledger commits) instead of flipping `require_authenticated` to `false` repo-wide, which drops enforcement against forged/unsigned writes.
evidence: docs/identity.md:133-135 `The merge-gate is the real control. "rebar verify-authorship" re-verifies every in-scope mutating event's signature ...`
docs/identity.md:149-151 `The gate exits non-zero (blocking the change) only when require_authenticated is on and any in-scope event is not verified; advisory (exit 0) when off.`

src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:543-550 `if not required: ... return 0` — with the flag off, ALL non-verified verdicts (including bad-signature forgeries and unsigned) are reported but not enforced.

rebar.toml:87-90 source #1 is a GENUINELY unsigned write: `a bot-identity completion-verified close emits PASS verdicts ... runs with NO resolvable identity.signing_key, so finalize_event writes them unsigned` — not a tooling false-positive.
rebar.toml comment (removed) stated the enforced posture's purpose: `a forged / unsigned / wrong-key write cannot land on main` — precisely the capability being disabled.

.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:214-215 `Unset ⇒ events are written unsigned (verify-identity is advisory until require_authenticated flips on)` — an active CI writer path that produces unsigned events now lands unblocked.
advisory.finding: Flipping `identity.require_authenticated` to `false` converts the CI merge-gate from enforcing to advisory (exit 0), removing the ONLY control that blocks forged (`bad-signature`), `unsigned`, and wrong-key writes from landing on `main`. The rollback is justified by two root causes, but only one (`key_not_valid_at_era`, source #2) is a plausible tooling false-positive; source #1 is a genuinely unsigned bot write. Disabling the whole gate (rather than scoping an exemption for the reducer-ignored sidecar types / the null-ledger re-resolution) drops enforcement against real forgeries/unsigned writes going forward.
scenarios: The reconcile-bridge bot runs with REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY unset (reconcile-bridge.yml:214) and writes unsigned in-scope events that now merge to main with no gate failure.
An actor with tickets-branch write access commits a forged (`bad-signature`) authorship event; the advisory gate reports it but exits 0, so it lands on main.
